name: Jerry Douglas
sources: Mix — Willie Nelson / Alison Krauss & Union Station with Jerry Douglas (https://www.mixonline.com/live-sound/willie-nelson-and-alison-krauss-and-union-station-jerry-douglas-425585)
notes: The dobro idiom's defining voice and the bluegrass wing's most-used producer, and flagship here because the research rates it high-medium with role, era, awards and production roster all sourced. The section's own scope note says why this entry looks the way it does: "in this archetype the producer role is largely occupied by instrumental specialists — the players whose parts are the train beat when there is no drum kit, and who also produce records. Each entry below is written as a parameter set for the part they contribute, because that is what the engine needs." His board is stated as a default: the records he produces (Alison Krauss, Del McCoury Band, Nashville Bluegrass Band, Steep Canyon Rangers, The Earls of Leicester) are "drummerless or brush-only by default — his production signature is the ensemble train beat". The section states the rule this half of the roster turns on: "the train beat is an ensemble function, not a drum part" — the banjo roll carries the continuous subdivision, the mandolin chop supplies the backbeat, and the upright bass supplies the two-beat kick. So the drum block is brush-range throughout — `velocityTiers` accent 80–96 against ghost 38–54, `kick` [1,2] on anchors 1 and 3, the hat on quarters and not continuous, `percs` at −10 dB, `fills` at 16/16 — and `snare.offGridMs` −5 is the grammar block's anticipated placement. Keys follow the one hard instrument constraint the entry gives: the dobro is tuned to an open G chord, "which sets the harmonic bias of every record he plays on: G, D, A and E read as open positions and everything else is barred, so G-family keys dominate his catalogue and modal ♭VII figures fall naturally under the bar", hence the key weights and the ♭VII family at weight 4. The melody block is the dobro's own parametric identity: "slide-only pitch — every note is approached by a glissando, so model portamento on entry to sustained notes (unlike everything else in this archetype, which forbids glides)" — legato articulation and a descending, step-heavy line are as close as the melody block gets, since portamento-on-entry has no field here. He "answers vocal phrases in 2-bar units and takes 8- or 16-bar breaks in the rotation", which is `phraseBars` weighted to 2 and a countermelody at −12 with a quarter-note echo offset. ⚠ INFERRED: velocity tiers, the −5 ms offset, `percs` contents, `bpm.mode` 120 (the entry states the whole archetype range, 65–210, and no centre) and every melody, countermelody and bassline number. ⚠ The entry marks the dobro tuning specifically: "[LOW-CONF] on the tuning specifics — sourced as instrument convention, not from his own words", and that flag carries to the key weights above. ⚠ The documented taste for repertoire-project records is "a stylistically locked project-level preset rather than per-song variation", which is a project constraint this schema has no field for.
